messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthsync.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: embedding job failures (bulk)

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Quick heads up — since the upgrade to runtime v1.8 our nightly bulk-embedding job (HealthSync batch ID 20260915) started seeing intermittent disconnects and OOM-style failures during the large-batch path. We attached a minimal repro and a trimmed log snippet; you can see the sequence where the client gets a 502 then the job restarts and later sees a "kv-cache invalidation" message in the runtime logs. This is blocking a production rollout we planned for next week.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with any recent kernel selection or KV cache changes in v1.8? If you have a temporary mitigation we can apply on our side (batch size cap, header toggle, etc.) that would be great. We can also give access to a staging workspace if helpful.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior SRE, HealthSync Labs

Attachments: healthsync_repro.tar.gz (repro scripts), redwood-error-log-20260915.txt (trimmed runtime logs)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: embedding job failures (bulk)

Forwarding HealthSync repro + logs. Summary: failures show up only on large-batch path (>= 2k tokens) after 30–45 minutes of sustained throughput; they sometimes manifest as 502 to client then runtime logs show a memory assertion around kv-cache invalidation. Not seen on small-batch runs.

Customer is on a Dedicated trial; this is blocking their production go-live. Customer asks for a workaround asap and wants timeline for a permanent fix in next patch.

Key asks for Eng: 1) reproduce locally using provided script, 2) capture full trace when it occurs, 3) confirm whether recent kernel selection or continuous-batching changes touched the KV cache invalidation path.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Sales Engineering Manager
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: embedding job failures (bulk)

I pulled the repro and ran it in a stripped-down staging cluster (rundir v1.8, n1-gpu). Initial observations: the sequence looks like an edge-case in the KV cache eviction path when continuous batching combines many short-lived requests into a single upstream kernel call. When the combined sequence length exceeds our internal buffer heuristic the code attempts an aggressive KV invalidation that races with the async flush — that can trigger a memory accounting assertion and cause the worker to return 502.

Short-term mitigations we tried that reduced the failure rate:
- disable continuous_batching (runtime flag) on the worker -> repro passes for 6+ runs
- reduce client max_batch_tokens to <= 1024 -> repro frequency drops dramatically
- set prefetch.enabled=false in the client -> also reduces frequency but increases latency

Action plan:
1) Capture full trace with X-Redwood-Trace (Soojin — please ask the customer to attach trace ids for the next failure).
2) Create a SUP ticket and assign a 1.8-patch hotfix branch to guard the KV invalidation with an extra refcount check.
3) On dedicated clusters, we can roll a policy to set continuous_batching=false for HealthSync as a temporary ACL.

I’ll open the SUP now and paste repro results.
— Dev
Runtime Engineer
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: embedding job failures (bulk)

Thanks Dev — good analysis. I sketched a minimal guard for the eviction path that should be safe for v1.8 and low-risk to cherry-pick. Proposal and timeline:
- Create hotfix branch off v1.8 and include eviction-refcount-guard patch (ETA: 24–48 hours)
- Publish a canary to a small subset of dedicated capacity and HealthSync staging (ETA: next business day morning)
- If canary stable, roll to production clusters for HealthSync by EOD + rollback window.

Customer-facing mitigations we should offer immediately:
- Apply per-customer runtime override: continuous_batching=false (low-risk, no code change)
- Share SDK workaround: set max_batch_tokens=1024 and prefetch.enabled=false (tradeoffs noted)

Soojin/Marissa — please confirm which option the customer prefers; I’ll prioritize the hotfix once we have sign-off. Also, I linked the SUP ticket with the HubSpot deal and added the canary playbook.
— Karthik
Platform Lead (Serving Runtime)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: embedding job failures (bulk)

Tom — update from our side: we can offer two immediate options and we’ve opened SUP-2389 for a hotfix:
1) Temporary config: we can set continuous_batching=false for your dedicated pool today (no code change). This should stop the failure mode while we validate the patch.
2) SDK workaround: set max_batch_tokens to 1024 and/or prefetch.enabled=false. We’ll document latency tradeoffs.

Karthik’s team will push a gated hotfix branch (eviction-refcount-guard) and run a canary in your staging account tomorrow morning. If that looks good we’ll promote to your dedicated region with a rollback window.

Please confirm which immediate option you want (1 or 2) and whether you can share X-Redwood-Trace ids if it happens again so we can attach the full trace to SUP-2389. We’ll update HubSpot and the SUP ticket as we progress.

Thanks — Soojin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
